method: One dossier per saved watchlist ticker and curated Opportunities Book idea, refreshed against the Fri 2026-09-11 close. Conviction is capped at 3 for companies that are not yet consistently profitable, and the reason is flagged in bear[].

DELL.why: Oracle reaffirmed roughly $95bn of AI capex on its Sep 10 print and named Dell as a beneficiary; Dell closed +11.98% at 567.29, a fresh 52-week high, on top of the $95bn AI-server backlog it disclosed on Sep 2.
bull: Record $95.0bn AI-server backlog disclosed Sep 2, with the order pipeline still widening
RBC initiated coverage Sep 11 at Outperform with a $640 target, ~13% above Friday's close
Oracle's capex pledge converts AI announcements into hardware purchase orders, and Dell and HPE are the named suppliers
bear: Server assembly is a thin-margin business: backlog dollars convert to far less gross profit than the headline suggests
Up 415% off its 52-week low of 110.22 — positioning is crowded and a single capex wobble unwinds it fast
A Sep 16 rate hike would hit the most-extended momentum names first
DELL.inv: Thesis breaks if hyperscaler or Oracle capex guidance is cut, or the backlog stops converting to revenue.
DELL.thesis: A (85.5/100). It closed AT its 52-week high, which is the worst possible entry. Let it digest: wait for a pullback toward 545 that holds, or a weekly close above 568 on continued volume, and size small into the Sep 16 Fed decision.

ANET.why: Rose 5.61% to 199.59 in a targeted rotation into networking — Cisco +3.1%, Ciena +4.5%, F5 +3.2%, Viavi +4.3% the same session. Money is buying the switching layer of the AI build, not tech broadly.
bull: Best-in-class Ethernet switching share as AI clusters standardise on Ethernet over InfiniBand
Sits only 7.1% below its 52-week high of 214.89 with genuine earnings behind the move, not multiple expansion alone
Gross margins far above the server assemblers benefiting from the same capex wave
bear: Customer concentration in a small number of hyperscalers
Merchant silicon competition from Broadcom-based white-box switching compresses pricing over time
Friday's 5.6% move was a sector rotation it did not earn alone
ANET.inv: Thesis breaks on evidence of hyperscalers shifting to white-box switching, or a close below the stop.
ANET.thesis: B+ (75.9/100). The move was sector-wide rather than Arista-specific, so it can give back quickly. Wait for it to hold above ~197 for a few sessions, or buy the entry near 193.6 if the networking bid persists past the FOMC.

VRT.why: Gained 3.60% to 257.06 on the same Oracle-capex read-through — Vertiv sells the power and thermal gear every one of those racks needs. Still 32.3% below its 52-week high of 379.94.
bull: Thermal and power management is a bottleneck in high-density AI racks, not a commodity
32.3% off its high while DELL makes new highs — the cheapest way to own the same capex dollar
Liquid-cooling attach rates rise with every generation of denser accelerators
bear: Deeply cyclical: order books can reverse faster than the market expects
Competition from Schneider and Eaton in the same electrical content
A rate hike raises the financing cost of the data centres it sells into
VRT.inv: Thesis breaks if AI data-centre orders decelerate or it closes below 226.2.
VRT.thesis: C+ (62.7/100). It is the laggard of the AI-hardware trio, which cuts both ways. Wait for a close back above ~265 to confirm it has joined the move, then buy near 249.3; do not buy it purely because it looks cheap against DELL.

NVDA.why: Closed flat (-0.03% at 218.29) on a session when Dell rose 11.98% and Arista 5.61%. The market is currently paying for who assembles and connects the AI build rather than for the silicon inside it — a rotation within the trade, not out of it.
bull: Oracle's ~$95bn capex pledge and Dell's $95bn backlog are orders that largely convert into Nvidia silicon
Reverse-DCF implies the price needs a 10-year free-cash-flow CAGR that its current backlog can plausibly support
Sits 7.7% below its 52-week high while the hardware chain it feeds makes new highs
bear: Revenue concentrated in a handful of hyperscalers plus Oracle
A Sep 16 hike compresses multiples on the longest-duration growth first
Custom accelerators from Broadcom and the hyperscalers chip at the merchant share over time
NVDA.inv: Thesis breaks if hyperscaler capex guidance is cut, or on a close below 192.1.
NVDA.thesis: B (74.3/100). It has round-tripped 164 to 236 and back to 218. Do not chase into the Sep 16 Fed decision: wait for a daily close above ~225 with the semis complex confirming, then scale in near 211.7.

TSM.why: Rose 1.22% to 433.24, holding within 9.6% of its 52-week high. Every accelerator in the Oracle and Dell backlog is fabricated here, which makes TSMC the least substitutable link in the chain.
bull: Effective monopoly on leading-edge logic — there is no second source for 3nm and below at volume
Pricing power has improved as advanced packaging capacity stays the binding constraint
Held up on Friday while the index churned, a sign of quality bid
bear: Taiwan-strait geopolitical risk is unhedgeable and not in the price
Capital intensity is enormous and rises each node
ADR holders wear currency and withholding drag
TSM.inv: Thesis breaks on a Taiwan escalation or evidence of leading-edge order cuts.
TSM.thesis: B (72.5/100). It is behaving well but the Sep 16 Fed decision is an unhedged event. Buy near 420.2 on any macro-driven dip rather than at the high; a close below 400 would say the AI-capex read-through is failing.

AVGO.why: Barely moved (+0.32% to 361.99) despite the Oracle capex news, and still sits 26.9% below its 52-week high of 495 — the widest gap between disclosed AI numbers and share price in the book.
bull: Its September quarter showed AI semiconductor revenue growing triple digits with a multi-year AI guide stepping up sharply
Custom accelerator programmes with hyperscalers are the direct beneficiary of the capex Oracle just reaffirmed
27% below its high while DELL makes new highs on the same underlying demand
bear: VMware software integration carries execution and customer-churn risk
Leverage from the VMware deal matters more if the Fed hikes on Sep 16
Custom-silicon revenue is lumpy and programme-dependent
AVGO.inv: Thesis breaks if custom-accelerator design wins are lost to a competitor, or on a close below 318.6.
AVGO.thesis: B- (67.7/100). The dislocation is the point, but it needs a trigger. Accumulate near 351.1 on weakness; add only on a daily close back above ~375 that shows the custom-silicon story is being re-rated rather than ignored.

AMD.why: Rose 2.49% to 516.13, within 11.7% of its 52-week high, as the AI-infrastructure bid broadened past Nvidia. The MI-series is now a credible second source at exactly the moment hyperscalers want one.
bull: Hyperscalers actively want a second accelerator source, and AMD is the only merchant alternative at scale
Server CPU share gains continue to compound quietly alongside the AI story
+2.49% on Sep 11 shows it participates in the capex read-through
bear: Software ecosystem still lags CUDA by a wide margin
Valuation leaves little room — the reverse-DCF is not meaningful here, so the 48 is a judgement call
Gross margins on accelerators sit well below Nvidia's
AMD.inv: Thesis breaks if MI-series design wins slip or it closes below 454.2.
AMD.thesis: B (71.2/100). It has tripled off its 149.85 low, so the easy money is gone. Wait for a close above ~530 that holds, then buy near 500.6; avoid adding in the two sessions around the Sep 16 FOMC.

MU.why: Slipped 0.22% to 975.26 and now sits 22.3% below its 52-week high of 1255, giving back part of the memory melt-up. The DRAM and HBM pricing cycle is intact but the stock has run far ahead of it.
bull: HBM allocation for leading-edge is effectively sold out through end-2026
DRAM and NAND pricing has moved from commodity to shortage economics
Every accelerator shipped into the Oracle and Dell backlog carries Micron content
bear: Memory is the most violently cyclical business in semis — the cycle turns without warning
Up 560% off its 52-week low
the risk is no longer the business, it is the entry price
Korean competitors are adding capacity into the shortage
MU.inv: Thesis breaks on DRAM spot-price rollover or a close below 858.2.
MU.thesis: B- (67.9/100). This is the most volatile name in the book — it ran from 147.61 to 1255 inside a year. Do not add here. Wait for it to base above ~1000 for a week, then buy near 945.9; a close under 900 means the memory trade is unwinding.

ASML.why: Added 0.64% to 1698.30, still 15.1% below its 52-week high. Every leading-edge wafer in the AI build requires its lithography, but orders are lumpy and the stock has lagged the chain it enables.
bull: Monopoly on EUV lithography — there is literally no alternative supplier
Leading-edge capacity expansion is the physical precondition for every AI accelerator shipped
High-NA transition extends the monopoly another technology generation
bear: Order intake is lumpy and a single quarter can badly miss
Export-control exposure to China revenue remains a policy risk
15% off the high while the demand story strengthened — the market is questioning order timing
ASML.inv: Thesis breaks on a leading-edge capex cut from TSMC or Samsung, or a close below 1528.5.
ASML.thesis: B- (68.4/100). Lagging is not the same as cheap here. Buy near 1647.3 on weakness; a close back above ~1750 would confirm the semicap group is following the logic names higher.

ALAB.why: Rose 2.35% to 291.22 but remains 41.7% below its 52-week high of 499.48 — the sharpest de-rating in the AI complex. It sells the connectivity silicon that links accelerators to memory and CPUs.
bull: Connectivity bottlenecks worsen as clusters scale, which is exactly its addressable problem
PCIe and CXL content per accelerator rises each generation
41.7% off the high while the underlying AI build accelerates
bear: Small, single-theme company with concentrated customers
Valuation remains high even after a 42% drawdown — the 35 is judgement, not a DCF output
Competition from Broadcom in the same connectivity layer is direct and well funded
ALAB.inv: Thesis breaks on a design-in loss to Broadcom or a close below 238.8.
ALAB.thesis: C- (54.8/100). Down 42% from the high is either an opportunity or a warning, and the tape has not decided. Only take a starter position near 283.9, and require a close above ~310 before adding. Speculative sizing for a reason.

MSFT.why: Added 0.65% to 495.63, sitting 10.5% below its 52-week high. It is both the largest AI capex spender and the largest beneficiary, which makes it the most defensive way to own the theme heading into a possible rate hike.
bull: Azure AI revenue is real, recurring and disclosed, unlike most AI monetisation claims
Fortress balance sheet means a Sep 16 rate hike is a multiple event, not a solvency one
Reverse-DCF implies a growth rate the enterprise franchise has met before
bear: Enormous AI capex is depressing free cash flow while returns remain unproven
Long-duration software de-rates first when the 10-year sits at 4.96%
Law of large numbers — growth necessarily decelerates from here
MSFT.inv: Thesis breaks on Azure growth deceleration below the mid-20s, or a close below 441.1.
MSFT.thesis: B- (69.9/100). There is no urgency here. Buy near 480.8 on macro weakness; treat any Fed-driven drawdown toward the 200-day as the opportunity rather than the risk, given the balance sheet.

GOOGL.why: Rose 1.77% to 338.50 in Friday's Communication Services-led rebound, still 17.2% below its 52-week high. Cheapest of the mega-cap platforms on the reverse-DCF despite owning its own AI silicon and model stack.
bull: Owns the full stack — TPUs, models, cloud and distribution — which no competitor matches
Comm Services led Friday's rebound, and Alphabet was a primary beneficiary
Reverse-DCF implies the lowest growth burden of the mega-cap platforms
bear: Search monetisation faces genuine disruption from conversational AI interfaces
Regulatory and antitrust overhang persists across multiple jurisdictions
Capex intensity has stepped up sharply without clear incremental return yet
GOOGL.inv: Thesis breaks on evidence of search query-share loss showing up in revenue, or a close below 304.7.
GOOGL.thesis: B- (68.8/100). Buy near 328.3 rather than chasing Friday's bounce. A close above ~350 would confirm the Comm Services rotation has legs; below 305 the search-disruption bear case is being priced.

META.why: Added 0.57% to 648.03 and remains 18.1% below its 52-week high of 790.80. It is spending like a hyperscaler without selling cloud, which is why it has lagged the rest of the group through the capex debate.
bull: Advertising remains a high-margin cash machine funding everything else
18% below its high — the capex concern is substantially priced in
AI-driven ad targeting improvements show up directly in revenue per user
bear: Capex is enormous with no external revenue line to justify it, unlike the cloud players
Reality Labs continues to consume cash with no visible path to return
Regulatory risk across the EU and US remains live
META.inv: Thesis breaks if capex guidance rises again without a revenue offset, or on a close below 576.7.
META.thesis: B- (65.1/100). Weakest catalyst in the mega-cap group right now. Buy only near 628.6 on a macro flush, and wait for a quarter that shows capex flattening before adding; a close under 580 says the spending concern is winning.

NOW.why: Rose 1.04% to 132.53 but sits 31.9% below its 52-week high of 194.73 — a textbook long-duration software de-rating with the 10-year at 4.96% and a hike likely on Sep 16.
bull: Enterprise workflow contracts are sticky with very high net revenue retention
31.9% off its high purely on rates, not on execution
AI agent products are landing in an installed base that already pays
bear: Highest rate-sensitivity in the book — a Sep 16 hike hits this first and hardest
Seat-based pricing models face questions as AI agents replace seats
Still not cheap in absolute terms despite the drawdown
NOW.inv: Thesis breaks on net-retention deterioration or a close below 117.9.
NOW.thesis: C+ (60.4/100). Do not catch this ahead of the Fed. Wait until after the Sep 16 decision and require a daily close above ~142 with software participating; then buy near 128.6. The de-rating is rate-driven and rates are the thing that has not settled.

PANW.why: Fell 2.32% to 330.65, one of the weaker large-caps on an up day, and sits 17.1% below its 52-week high. Security spending is resilient but the multiple is not, with the 2-year at 4.63%.
bull: Security budgets are the last line item cut in an enterprise slowdown
Platform consolidation strategy is winning multi-product deals
17% below its high with the underlying spending environment intact
bear: Fell 2.32% on a +0.86% S&P day — relative weakness is the tell
Long-duration multiple compresses further if the Fed hikes on Sep 16
Competitive intensity from CrowdStrike and Microsoft is rising
PANW.inv: Thesis breaks on billings deceleration or a close below 294.3.
PANW.thesis: C+ (60.8/100). It fell on a day the market rose, which is a warning rather than a discount. Stay out until it closes back above ~345; then buy near 320.7. Do not average into relative weakness before the FOMC.

XOM.why: Rose 0.46% to 165.99 with Brent up 8.7% on the week before Friday's 2.5% pullback. Energy led the S&P for a second consecutive week on Strait of Hormuz supply fear.
bull: Brent +8.7% on the week with supply risk from Hormuz still unresolved
Integrated model captures both upstream price and downstream crack spreads
Reverse-DCF implies a growth rate that current strip pricing comfortably funds
bear: The entire move is a geopolitical premium — diplomatic progress removes it quickly
Friday's 2.5% Brent pullback on talks hopes shows how fast it unwinds
Energy equities lagged the crude move, suggesting the market doubts durability
XOM.inv: Thesis breaks on a Hormuz de-escalation that takes Brent back under $80, or a close below 147.7.
XOM.thesis: B+ (75.8/100). Energy has run hard for two weeks on a geopolitical premium that can deflate on a headline. Buy near 161.0 on any diplomacy-driven pullback rather than at the top of the range; the trigger is oil holding above $95 Brent, not the equity chart.

CVX.why: Set a fresh 52-week high at 214.06 on Sep 11 — its second in three sessions — closing +0.61%. Brent settling above $101 on Sep 9 for the first time since May was the trigger.
bull: Fresh 52-week high on Sep 11, the second in three sessions — sustained institutional buying
Strongest balance sheet among the majors, so it compounds through the cycle
Permian and Guyana volume growth is independent of the oil price spike
bear: Trading 1.5% from its 52-week high on a premium the market may not keep paying
Friday's 2.5% Brent pullback on diplomacy hopes is the direct risk
Energy's two-week leadership makes it a crowded rotation
CVX.inv: Thesis breaks on Brent sustainably below $80, or a close below 190.5.
CVX.thesis: B+ (79.5/100). It just printed a 52-week high, so patience matters more than conviction. Buy near 205.5 on a pullback that holds; chasing a name at its high on a geopolitical premium into an FOMC is the error to avoid.

COP.why: Closed 137.35, just 1.1% below its 52-week high of 138.89, after joining CVX and VLO at annual highs on Sep 9. Pure upstream leverage to the Hormuz premium.
bull: Highest upstream torque to crude of the three energy majors held here
Hit a 52-week high on Sep 9 as Brent cleared $101 for the first time since May
Low-cost, long-duration resource base with disciplined capital return
bear: No refining hedge — a pure price bet with no downstream offset
1.1% from its 52-week high on a geopolitical premium
A Hormuz resolution would hit this hardest of the energy names
COP.inv: Thesis breaks on Brent below $80 or a close below 123.6.
COP.thesis: B+ (78.2/100). The purest oil-price beta in the book and it is at its high. Wait for a pullback to near 131.9 rather than buying the breakout; require Brent to hold above $95 or the whole setup is invalid.

VLO.why: Rose 1.29% to 390.42, its fifth straight weekly gain and near a 52-week high, with the WTI 3-2-1 crack spread above $64 a barrel — the highest since 2022 and more than three times its $19 long-run median.
bull: WTI 3-2-1 crack above $64 versus a $19 long-run median — extraordinary refining margins
Fifth consecutive weekly gain with refiners VLO, PSX, PBF, MPC, DINO and DK all at 52-week highs on Sep 11
Refining capacity is structurally tight with no new US builds
bear: Crack spreads at 3.4x their long-run median are a mean-reverting input, not a permanent one
Commodity processor with no pricing power of its own
Hormuz diplomacy would compress both crude and cracks
VLO.inv: Thesis breaks on the 3-2-1 crack falling under $45, or a close below 351.4.
VLO.thesis: B+ (76.7/100). The crack spread is the entire thesis and it is at a generational extreme, which means it mean-reverts. Buy only near 374.8 on a pullback, and treat a crack spread back under $45 as the exit signal regardless of the chart.

SLB.why: Flat at 56.06 (+0.09%) and 7.3% below its 52-week high, lagging badly while CVX, COP and VLO printed annual highs. Services follow the capex decision, not the spot price, and that decision has not been made yet.
bull: Levered to the upstream capex cycle that sustained $100 oil eventually triggers
Lagged the producers badly, so it has not priced the geopolitical premium
International and offshore exposure where activity is least US-shale-dependent
bear: Producers have been disciplined — high prices may not translate into capex this cycle
Barely moved during a two-week energy rally, which is itself a negative tell
A Hormuz resolution removes the catalyst before it ever arrives
SLB.inv: Thesis breaks if upstream capex budgets stay flat through the next guidance round, or on a close below 49.3.
SLB.thesis: B (71.0/100). Services lag producers by design — the capex response to $100 oil comes later. Wait for evidence of upstream budget increases, then buy near 54.6; a close above ~58 would signal the market is pricing that second wave.

JPM.why: Rose 0.76% to 356.23, within 2.8% of its 52-week high, as the market moved to price an 81-90% chance of a Fed hike on Sep 16. Banks are one of the few groups that benefit from higher short rates.
bull: Higher policy rates expand net interest margin — a hike is a direct earnings tailwind
The 10-year at 4.96% versus the 2-year at 4.63% means the curve is positively sloped, not inverted
Fortress balance sheet with best-in-class credit underwriting
bear: Credit costs rise with a lag if higher rates slow the economy
2.8% from its 52-week high leaves little margin for disappointment
Banks are excluded from the reverse-DCF, so the 66 is judgement not a computed output
JPM.inv: Thesis breaks on credit deterioration in card or commercial books, or a close below 317.0. Valuation is a judgement score: banks are excluded from the DCF because a free-cash-flow growth solve is not meaningful for a balance-sheet business.
JPM.thesis: B+ (78.1/100). It is close to its high and the hike is largely priced, so the reward is in confirmation not anticipation. Buy near 345.5 on a pullback; the trigger is the Sep 16 decision landing as expected and the curve staying positively sloped.

GS.why: Rose 0.92% to 1029.18, 10.8% below its 52-week high. Capital markets activity benefits from the AI capex boom financing itself — Oracle's spending has to be funded somewhere.
bull: Debt and equity issuance to fund AI infrastructure flows straight to fee revenue
Higher rates support net interest income in its financing book
10.8% below its high while the deal environment improves
bear: Capital markets revenue is inherently cyclical and lumpy
A rate hike that slows the economy closes the issuance window
Excluded from the reverse-DCF — the 64 is judgement, not computed
GS.inv: Thesis breaks if the issuance window closes or it closes below 916.0. Valuation is a judgement score — investment banks are excluded from the DCF for the same reason as JPM.
GS.thesis: B (72.2/100). Less directly rate-levered than JPM, so the Sep 16 event matters less. Buy near 998.3 on weakness; a close above ~1075 would confirm the capital-markets recovery is being re-rated rather than just hoped for.

DE.why: Slipped 0.32% to 675.74 but holds within 4.3% of its 52-week high — remarkable relative strength for a cyclical with the 2-year at 4.63% and a hike likely.
bull: Holding within 4.3% of its 52-week high while rate-sensitive cyclicals de-rate
Precision agriculture technology is a genuine recurring-revenue transition
Analyst support is strong, with Baird and Evercore ISI both at Outperform with $800 and $813 targets
bear: Farm income is under pressure and equipment is the most deferrable purchase there is
A Sep 16 hike raises financing costs for the customer, not just the company
4.3% from the high leaves little room if the ag cycle turns
DE.inv: Thesis breaks on a farm-income-driven order collapse or a close below 618.3.
DE.thesis: B (74.3/100). It is holding near highs despite the rate backdrop, which is the bull case and also the risk. Buy near 655.5 on a pullback; a close below 620 would say the farm-economy bear case is finally biting.

ETN.why: Rose 3.96% to 425.37, one of Friday's stronger large-cap moves, on the same Oracle capex read-through — data centres need electrical distribution before they need chips. Sits 11.0% below its 52-week high.
bull: +3.96% on Sep 11 as data-centre electrical content was re-rated alongside Dell and Vertiv
Electrical infrastructure is a physical bottleneck for AI capacity, with multi-year backlogs
Diversified across aerospace, vehicle and industrial end markets, not a pure AI bet
bear: Reverse-DCF implies a demanding long-run growth rate for an industrial
Cyclical exposure if a Sep 16 hike slows broader industrial activity
11% below its high despite the strongest end-market demand in its history
ETN.inv: Thesis breaks on data-centre order deceleration or a close below 378.6.
ETN.thesis: B (71.9/100). A strong move without a company-specific catalyst can fade. Buy near 412.6; require it to hold above 415 through the FOMC week to confirm the electrification bid is durable rather than a one-day sympathy trade.

GE.why: Slipped 0.15% to 323.66, 16.8% below its 52-week high. Aftermarket engine services are about as insulated from a Fed hike as an industrial gets, but the name has drifted while energy and AI hardware led.
bull: Engine aftermarket is a decades-long annuity with very high margins
Air-traffic growth drives shop visits independent of the rate cycle
16.8% below its high with no deterioration in the underlying franchise
bear: Supply-chain constraints continue to limit engine delivery rates
Valuation already reflects much of the aftermarket story — the 50 is judgement
A rate hike pressures airline capex and fleet decisions
GE.inv: Thesis breaks on a sustained air-traffic decline or a close below 288.1.
GE.thesis: C+ (62.8/100). Nothing is forcing the move here. Accumulate near 313.9 on weakness rather than waiting for a breakout; the thesis is the aftermarket annuity, which does not need a catalyst to compound.

GEV.why: Rose 3.61% to 957.27 on the data-centre power theme, though it remains 20.0% below its 52-week high of 1195.94. Gas turbines and grid equipment are the hard constraint on AI capacity.
bull: +3.61% on Sep 11 as the data-centre power constraint was re-rated
Gas turbine order backlogs extend years out with pricing power
Grid equipment demand is structural and independent of the AI cycle
bear: Very high valuation even after a 20% drawdown — the 45 is a judgement score
Execution risk in the offshore wind segment continues
Long-cycle equipment orders are vulnerable if financing costs rise on Sep 16
GEV.inv: Thesis breaks on turbine order cancellations or a close below 842.4.
GEV.thesis: B- (65.2/100). It moved 3.6% on sympathy rather than news. Buy near 928.5; require a close above ~1000 to confirm the power-equipment bid is real. This is the most expensive way in the book to own electrification.

CEG.why: Fell 0.43% to 284.75 and sits 31.0% below its 52-week high of 412.70. The AI-power trade has broken down even as AI capex accelerates — a genuine divergence worth watching.
bull: Existing nuclear capacity is the only large-scale carbon-free baseload available today
Data-centre power demand is structural and rising with every announcement
31% below its high while the demand driver strengthened
bear: Fell on an up day during the strongest week yet for AI capex news — the tape disagrees
Power purchase agreement pricing is politically and regulatorily contested
A rate hike pressures capital-intensive utility valuations
CEG.inv: Thesis breaks on adverse PPA pricing decisions or a close below 253.4.
CEG.thesis: C- (54.0/100). The divergence is interesting but the tape is against it. Do not buy the drawdown yet: wait for a close back above ~300, then buy near 276.2. Falling 0.43% on an up day is not a bottom.

VST.why: Rose 0.90% to 148.38 but remains 32.5% below its 52-week high of 219.82, now sitting just 11.9% above its 52-week low. The AI-power trade has fully unwound here.
bull: Merchant power exposure to rising data-centre demand in constrained markets
32.5% below its high with the underlying electricity demand story intact
Nuclear and gas fleet positioned in the tightest capacity regions
bear: Only 11.9% above its 52-week low — the trend is clearly down
Merchant power earnings are volatile and hedge-dependent
The AI-power theme has now failed to work for months despite accelerating AI capex
VST.inv: Thesis breaks on a power-price decline in ERCOT or PJM, or a close below 134.0.
VST.thesis: C- (51.4/100). This is closer to its 52-week low than its high, so the trend is down. Require a close above ~158 before doing anything; then buy near 144.7. Do not average into a broken theme before it turns.

CCJ.why: Fell 0.76% to 96.68, 28.5% below its 52-week high, in a week when UBS cut NuScale to Sell and SMR fell 15.67%. The nuclear complex is being repriced from story to schedule.
bull: Uranium supply remains structurally short against restart and newbuild demand
Long-term contracting prices have reset materially higher
Westinghouse stake provides fuel-cycle and services exposure beyond mining
bear: The nuclear complex de-rated hard this week — UBS cut SMR to Sell, and SMR fell 15.67%
Mining execution and production guidance have disappointed before
28.5% below its high with the theme losing narrative support
CCJ.inv: Thesis breaks on spot uranium weakness or a close below 87.4.
CCJ.thesis: C- (51.3/100). The whole nuclear theme is de-rating on timeline scepticism. Stay out until it closes above ~103. Then buy near 94.3 with speculative sizing only; UBS's SMR downgrade logic applies to the fuel cycle too.

LLY.why: Fell 0.65% to 1115.70, 13.7% below its 52-week high, as healthcare continued to lag. The incretin franchise is the strongest product cycle in pharma, but the reverse-DCF asks a great deal of it.
bull: The incretin franchise has genuine multi-year volume growth ahead of it
Manufacturing capacity expansion is finally easing the supply constraint
Oral formulations open a materially larger addressable population
bear: Reverse-DCF implies the most demanding long-run growth rate in the book
Competitive pressure from Novo and a long tail of clinical entrants
Drug-pricing policy risk remains a live political issue
LLY.inv: Thesis breaks on incretin share loss or a close below 1002.0.
LLY.thesis: C+ (64.1/100). The business is not the question; the price is. Buy near 1082.2 on weakness, and treat the reverse-DCF's demanding implied growth rate as the reason to size this at core rather than maximum weight.

UNH.why: Fell 2.37% to 379.09, among the worst large-cap performers on an up day, and sits 17.9% below its 52-week high. Medical cost trend remains the unresolved problem.
bull: Cheapest name in the book on the judgement valuation score at 72
Scale in both insurance and Optum services is structurally advantaged
17.9% below its high with a large installed membership base
bear: -2.37% on an up day — clear relative weakness and a distribution pattern
Medical cost trend has repeatedly surprised to the upside
Regulatory and reimbursement risk in Medicare Advantage is unresolved
